title: Argument from reason: conditional propositions about future contingents are determinately true or false
source_text: XV. Praeterea multis argumentis ex ratione ductis probari posse putant talem scientiam in Deo reperiri. Et primo quidem inde quod in propositionibus de futuro contingenti sub aliqua conditione determinata est veritas, vel falsitas, non minus quam in propositionibus de iis quae sunt absolute futura; ac proinde sunt illae quoque scientiae divinae objectum: quandoquidem nulla veritas latere potest intellectum infinitum, qualis divinus est. Propositiones autem de futuris contingentibus sub aliqua conditione determinate veras, vel falsas esse, ex eo conficitur quod inter eas vera potest esse contradictio, haud secus ac inter eas quae sunt de rebus absolute futuris. Siquidem prorsus haec sibi contradicunt, Si Petrus in talibus circumstantiis ponatur, peccabit, Et, Non si Petrus in talibus circumstantiis ponatur, peccabit. In omnibus autem contradictoriis, necesse est alteram partem contradictionis veram, alteram falsam esse.
pass_a_gloss: XV. Moreover they think it can be proved by many arguments drawn from reason that such knowledge is found in God. And first indeed from this, that in propositions concerning a future contingent under some condition there is determinate truth, or falsity, no less than in propositions concerning those things which are absolutely future; and therefore those too are the object of divine knowledge: since no truth can lie hidden from an infinite intellect, such as the divine is. But that propositions concerning future contingents under some condition are determinately true, or false, is concluded from this that between them there can be true contradiction, no otherwise than between those which are about things absolutely future. Since these plainly contradict each other, If Peter be placed in such circumstances, he will sin, And, Not if Peter be placed in such circumstances, will he sin. But in all contradictories, it is necessary that one part of the contradiction be true, the other false.
pass_b_english: They also think many arguments from reason prove that God has such knowledge. The first is this. Propositions about a future contingent under some condition have determinate truth or falsity, just as much as propositions about things that will absolutely happen. So they too are objects of God's knowledge, since no truth can be hidden from an infinite intellect, which the divine intellect is.

That propositions about future contingents under a condition are determinately true or false follows from the fact that there can be genuine contradiction between them, just as between propositions about things that will absolutely happen. These two plainly contradict each other: 'If Peter is placed in such circumstances, he will sin' and 'It is not the case that if Peter is placed in such circumstances, he will sin.' In every pair of contradictories one side must be true and the other false.
